subject.title: fix: order ambient transcript watermarks by decimal ids

question: What ordering contract should ambient transcript watermarks use when equal-timestamp message IDs are opaque or mixed with canonical decimal IDs?
rationale: Only the channel or transcript source can establish whether opaque identifiers have an order; choosing lexical collation changes persisted replay boundaries and cannot be justified from the current tests alone.

options.title: Require source-defined ordering
options.body: Use a documented per-source monotonic cursor or comparator, and do not advance a same-timestamp watermark when an opaque ID lacks that contract.

options.title: Limit the feature to decimal IDs
options.body: Keep numeric comparison for canonical decimal identifiers and treat opaque equal-timestamp IDs as non-orderable until a source-specific cursor exists.

options.title: Adopt lexical ordering intentionally
options.body: Document lexical collation as the public cross-source contract and accept its replay-boundary behavior for existing opaque identifiers.

recommendation.title: Require source-defined ordering
recommendation.body: Use a documented per-source monotonic cursor or comparator, and do not advance a same-timestamp watermark when an opaque ID lacks that contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Their explicit participation in the earlier review is the only concrete routing signal for this unresolved ordering decision.
